# Setting up Claude Code {.unnumbered} Installation details change. If a command here fails, check the [Claude Code setup page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) first. Claude Code is an AI agentAn assistant that can read across a project’s files and, depending on its permission mode, edit them and run commands, such as Claude Code. An agent acts; a chat window only advises. that runs in the Terminal tab of RStudio or Positron. It reads the files in the project you start it from, edits them, and runs commands, including R scripts, asking your permission as it goes. Most participants at this level have not used a terminal much. You need very little of it: one command to start Claude Code, and the R console and Git pane for everything else. This chapter covers the minimum, and ends with a check that everything works before the workshop day. *⏱ ~30 minutes, best done before the workshop* ## Before you install: three questions 1. **Are you permitted to use it on this work?** Claude Code sends the files it reads, and the output of commands it runs, to Anthropic. Check your institution's policy, and your ethics approval and data agreements if you will use it near research data. [Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd) covers this in detail. 2. **Which account will you use?** You need one of: - a **Claude Pro or Max subscription**, signing in with your Claude.ai account; - a **Claude for Teams or Enterprise** seat, if your institution provides one; - a **Claude Console** account, which bills API use per request; - access through a cloud provider (Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI or Microsoft Foundry), if your institution has set this up. Check current prices on Anthropic's pricing page before you choose. 3. **Is your computer supported?** Claude Code requires macOS 13 or later, Windows 10 (version 1809) or later, or a recent Linux distribution. ## Step 1: Open the Terminal tab in your IDE Claude Code runs in the **Terminal** tab of RStudio or Positron, beside the R console: - **RStudio:** the **Terminal** tab next to the Console, or *Tools → Terminal → New Terminal*. - **Positron:** *Terminal → New Terminal*. When a project is open, its Terminal tab starts in the project's root folder, which is exactly where Claude Code needs to run. You never need to `cd` anywhere. **Which shell is it?** Look at the prompt: - it starts with `PS`: **PowerShell** (Windows); - it ends with `$`: **Git Bash** (Windows, RStudio's usual default), or bash or zsh (macOS, Linux). To change it: in RStudio, *Tools → Global Options → Terminal → New terminals open with*; in Positron, the drop-down beside **+** in the terminal panel. ## Step 2: Check git and R are reachable Claude Code runs R by calling `Rscript`, and it works best in a git repository. **In the terminal:** ```bash git --version Rscript --version ``` Both should print a version number. - **`git` not found:** install git. On Windows, install **Git for Windows**. - **`Rscript` not found (common on Windows):** R's folder is not on your `PATH`. In the R console, run `R.home("bin")` to see the folder, and add it to your `PATH` environment variable (Windows: search the Start menu for "Edit environment variables for your account", then edit **Path**). Then **quit and reopen RStudio or Positron**: its terminals keep the `PATH` they started with, so a new Terminal tab is not enough. ## Step 3: Install Claude Code **macOS or Linux.** In the terminal: ```bash curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ``` **Windows.** The installer runs in PowerShell. If your Terminal tab's prompt starts with `PS`, run this there; if it is Git Bash, open the **PowerShell** app from the Start menu for this one step: ```powershell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` **macOS with Homebrew** (alternative): ```bash brew install --cask claude-code ``` Then **quit and reopen RStudio or Positron**, open the Terminal tab and confirm the installation. **In the terminal:** ```bash claude --version ``` The native installer keeps Claude Code up to date in the background. Homebrew installations need to be updated by hand. On Windows, Claude Code runs its own commands in Git Bash if Git for Windows is installed, and in PowerShell if not; either works for this course. ## Before you sign in: prepare your workshop repository Set-up takes time on the day, so do these once beforehand. Step 6 then checks the result. 1. **Fork the workshop template, clone it and open it.** In the R console, `usethis::create_from_github("/", fork = TRUE)` does all three, and opens the project in a new RStudio or Positron window. Your instructor gives you the exact name. 2. **Restore the packages.** In the R console, run `renv::restore()` once. It installs the package versions recorded in the template's lockfileThe renv.lock file that records the R version and the exact package versions a project uses, so renv::restore() can rebuild the same environment., and can take several minutes. 3. **Check the skills folder.** Claude Code reads skillsA folder containing a SKILL.md file (and optionally scripts and templates) that an assistant loads only when it is invoked by name or judged relevant from its description. from `.claude/skills/`. If `.claude/skills/clean-with-codebook/SKILL.md` does not exist, copy the skill folders across in the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_copy( here::here(".agents", "skills"), here::here(".claude", "skills"), overwrite = TRUE ) ``` ::: Copying works the same on every system. On macOS or Linux you can instead create a symbolic linkA file-system entry that points to another folder or file, so one copy can appear in two places. On Windows, copying the folder is usually simpler., as [Block 5](11e-instructions-skills.qmd) describes. 4. **Commit**, using the Git pane (RStudio) or Source Control view (Positron), so that your fork has no uncommitted changes when the day starts. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Using Posit Assistant Posit Assistant needs no terminal install: it is built into RStudio and Positron, and you configure it there. It reads skills from `.agents/skills/` directly, so step 3 is not needed. Check that your account or provider key works before the day; the access note in [Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd) lists the options. ::: ## Your workshop repository Every block from Block 4 onwards works in this one repository. The template ships most of it; the files marked *you* are created during the day. ``` data/ raw/voles_metabolism.csv Blocks 2–5, 9 and 10 (one deliberate NA) raw/voles_raw.csv Block 7 (errors planted by your instructor) derived/ written by Block 7's cleaning docs/ data_note.md the data provider's note (Block 7) codebook.csv you, Block 7 ai-log.md you, from Block 4 scripts/ explore_voles.R Block 4 (exploratory, so unnumbered) 00_profile.R … 03_audit_cleaning.R Block 7: the cleaning pipeline 04_load_data.R, 05_analysis.R Block 9: the analysis functions/ load_voles.R, validate_voles.R, and summary_functions.R (Block 9) tests/ make_reference.R, test_cleaning.R fixtures/ the references you capture (Blocks 7 and 9) AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md you, Block 5 .agents/skills/, .claude/skills/ skills (copies of the same folders) .claude/settings.json the deny rules (read in Block 6) renv.lock the package versions ``` `.claude/settings.json` ships with the template. It holds the deny rulesA permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code’s built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files. that protect the raw data, the codebook, the checks and the references. You read and test it in [Block 6](11f-enforced-controls.qmd) rather than writing it. Scripts are numbered in the order they run, which is what the README in Block 10 reports as the run order. ## Step 4: Sign in With your workshop project open, start Claude Code in its Terminal tab. **In the terminal:** ```bash claude ``` If a Terminal tab was already open before you switched projects, it may still be in the old folder: close it and open a new one. On first launch, Claude Code opens a browser window. Sign in with the account you chose above. To switch accounts later, use `/logout` and `/login` inside Claude Code. :::{.callout-warning} **API keys.** If you use a Console API key, set it as the environment variable `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Many R users keep keys in `.Renviron`. Never commit that file. Add it to `.gitignore`. The template's settings already include the deny rule `Read(/.Renviron)` (see [Block 6](11f-enforced-controls.qmd)), but it covers only a `.Renviron` in the project folder, not the one in your home folder. If `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is already set for another tool, such as Posit Assistant, Claude Code may use it instead of your subscription, and you will be billed per request. Check which credential is in use under `/config`. ::: ## Step 5: Learn five things | To... | Do this | |---|---| | Start in your workshop repository | Open the project, then type `claude` in its Terminal tab | | Change how much it may do without asking | `Shift+Tab` cycles `default` → `acceptEdits` → `plan` | | Start in read-only planning mode | `claude --permission-mode plan` | | See which permission rules are active | `/permissions` | | Leave | `/exit`, or close the terminal | Each of these settings is a permission modeThe setting that decides how much Claude Code may do without asking: plan (read only), default (asks before edits and commands), acceptEdits (edits without asking) and bypassPermissions (never asks).. Every time it wants to edit a file or run a command in `default` mode, Claude Code asks first. Read each request before you approve it. The autonomy ladder in [Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd) explains what each mode allows, and the full [Claude Code quick reference](11-AI-programming-integrated.qmd#cc-quick-reference) in Block 1 adds how to interrupt it, approve a plan and start a new conversation. Always start Claude Code from your workshop project's Terminal tab. It works on the folder it starts in, and your project settings in `.claude/settings.json` are found relative to it. ### Where am I typing? {#where-am-i-typing} Four places look alike but run different things: | Where | What runs there | |---|---| | The Claude Code prompt, inside the Terminal tab | Your requests to Claude Code. A line starting `!` runs a shell command, and its output is added to the conversation, so it reaches the model too. | | The terminal's own prompt (`PS`, `$` or `%`), after `/exit` | Shell commands: `claude`, git, `Rscript` | | The R console | R code. Claude Code cannot see it, or anything you load there. | | The Git pane (RStudio) or Source Control view (Positron) | Git status, diffs, reverting and committing, on the same repository | While Claude Code is running, the Terminal tab belongs to it: anything you type there goes to Claude, not to the shell. So do your checking somewhere else. ### Checking work while Claude Code is running {#checking-work} Every block checks the agent's work in the same few ways, all from the R console or the Git pane, which work identically on Windows, macOS and Linux: | To check... | In the R console or Git pane | |---|---| | What changed | The Git pane: each changed file, and **Diff** to read the changes line by line. **Revert** undoes a change you did not want. | | That a script runs in a fresh R session | `callr::rscript(here::here("scripts", "name.R"))`, or *Session → Restart R* and then `source()` it | | That the tests pass in a fresh R session | `callr::r(\(d) testthat::test_dir(d), list(here::here("tests")))` | | That the packages match the lockfile | `renv::status()` | Each Claude Code `Rscript` call is a fresh R process too, so objects do not carry over between its commands, any more than they reach it from your console. :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## At the command line The same checks from a terminal (after `/exit`, or in a second Terminal tab): `git status`, `git diff`, `git restore `, `Rscript scripts/name.R`, `Rscript -e "testthat::test_dir('tests')"` and `Rscript -e "renv::status()"`. ::: ## Step 6: Check everything works :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Pre-workshop check (15 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Start state:** your workshop project is open in RStudio or Positron, and the Git pane shows no uncommitted changes. **1. Read-only.** Start in `plan` mode. **In the Terminal tab:** ```bash claude --permission-mode plan ``` **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text Describe the structure of this repository and what each top-level folder contains. Do not change anything. ``` Type `/exit`. The Git pane (or Source Control view) should show no changed files. **2. R is reachable.** Start `claude` again, in `default` mode. **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text Run Rscript -e "sessionInfo()" and show me the output. ``` Approve the command when asked. You should see your R version and loaded packages. If Claude Code reports that `Rscript` was not found, return to Step 2. **3. Project settings load.** Type `/permissions`. The deny rules from `.claude/settings.json`, which ships with the template, should be listed. If the list is empty, check that you started `claude` from the workshop project's Terminal tab. **4. The project is ready.** In the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} renv::status() file.exists(here::here(".claude", "skills", "clean-with-codebook", "SKILL.md")) callr::r(\(d) testthat::test_dir(d), list(here::here("tests"))) ``` ::: `renv::status()` should report no problems, `file.exists()` should return `TRUE`, and the tests should run with **no failures**: at this point almost every test is skipped, because each one waits for the block that creates its files. By 16:00 they will all run. **5. Inline completion works.** Open a new R script and type `# Calculate the mean of 1 to 100`. Grey suggested text should appear within a few seconds ([Block 2](11b-inline-completions.qmd) uses it first thing). **6. The checkpoint branches are there.** Open the branch menu in the Git pane (or Source Control view). You should see `block5-done`, `block7-done` and `block9-done`. If you fall behind on the day, you switch to one of these and carry on. Stay on `main` for now. **7. Bring evidence.** Copy the output of steps 2, 3 and 4 into a text file and bring it to the workshop. If any step failed, note the error message exactly. **You are done when** the Git pane shows no changes, `/permissions` lists the deny rules, and the tests run with no failures. **If it goes wrong:** for Claude Code problems, return to the step named in the error; for a changed file, use **Revert** in the Git pane; for package problems, run `renv::restore()` again and send the error to your instructor before the day. :::: ::: ## Where Claude Code fits among the course's tools | | Claude Code | Posit Assistant | GitHub Copilot | |---|---|---|---| | Where it runs | The Terminal tab of RStudio or Positron | Inside RStudio or Positron | Your editor, github.com, and GitHub's servers (cloud agent) | | What it sees | Project files, and output of commands it runs | Your live R session and project files | Open files; on github.com, the repository | | Instruction file | `CLAUDE.md` (importing `AGENTS.md`) | `AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | | Skills folder | `.claude/skills/` | `.agents/skills/` | `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.github/skills/` | The later blocks give instructions for Claude Code, with differences for Posit Assistant in collapsed boxes. ## Glossary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term definition
agent An assistant that can read across a project's files and, depending on its permission mode, edit them and run commands, such as Claude Code. An agent acts; a chat window only advises.
deny rule A permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code's built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files.
lockfile The renv.lock file that records the R version and the exact package versions a project uses, so renv::restore() can rebuild the same environment.
permission mode The setting that decides how much Claude Code may do without asking: plan (read only), default (asks before edits and commands), acceptEdits (edits without asking) and bypassPermissions (never asks).
skill A folder containing a SKILL.md file (and optionally scripts and templates) that an assistant loads only when it is invoked by name or judged relevant from its description.
symbolic link A file-system entry that points to another folder or file, so one copy can appear in two places. On Windows, copying the folder is usually simpler.
````` ::: ::: ## References - Claude Code documentation: *Advanced setup*, ; *Authentication*, ; *Permission modes*, .
